replication.target_description: Study 1A, Japanese sample: simple linear regression of mean face-likeness ratings over 35 test trials on continuous importance-of-religion score. Supplied outcome/predictor description differs as detailed in notes.

es.location: Study 1, Results and Discussion, canonical text L126; supplied locator p. 4 (no PDF supplied)
es.quote: A simple linear regression revealed that religiosity significantly predicted perceived face-likeness of stimulus images in Study 1A, F(1, 95) = 13.28, p < .001, and the standardized slope was statistically significant from zero, β = 0.35, t(95) = 3.64, p < .001

notes: Identity independently checked: title Being Watched by Anthropomorphized Objects Affects Charitable Donation in Religious People, author Yuki Miyazaki, first published 10 June 2017, Japanese Psychological Research 59(3), 221–229, DOI 10.1111/jpr.12158 (L15–48). Supplied Wiley HTML parse labels this an Original Article and contains Study 1 methods and results, not abstract-only evidence. No PDF supplied. Mapping uses explicit Study 1A/Japan and Study 1B/United States labels (L97–98, L106, L125–127), not input order or numeric matching. Study 1A explicitly identifies the Japanese sample and prints this standardized slope. No conversion. Exact target correspondence is flagged false: the supplied description specifies predefined-region identification and believer-group membership, whereas the source documents mean face-likeness ratings and continuous religiosity (L110–121). Retain this explicitly named study coefficient for parent review; no coefficient for a categorical region-identification test is established here. Confidence denotes literal coefficient transcription, not exact target equivalence. Same-test p < .001 is preserved in the evidence quote. Only es_value_r assigned; all other fields/sides are unassessed placeholders. No N calculation.
